rules: Do not begin a phase until all features in the previous phase are 'completed'.
A feature is only 'completed' when its acceptance_criteria are met AND npm run build / npm run lint pass clean.
Update 'status' and 'last_updated' fields directly in this file as work progresses.
Do not delete or renumber feature ids — append notes instead if scope changes.

features.name: Streak Counter UI + Loss Modal
features.description: Header streak display plus a modal shown when a streak has been lost.
acceptance_criteria: Modal triggers correctly when streak state indicates a break since last session
Counter updates reactively from store state
features.notes: Break detection lives in a new store action, evaluateStreakOnLoad() (lib/streak.ts's daysSinceLastCompletion does calendar-day math), called once from a new components/gamification/ProgressInitializer.tsx (mounted in app/layout.tsx, replacing NavShell's old hydrate() call — hydration now lives there too). Caught and fixed a real bug during verification: React Strict Mode double-invokes mount effects in dev, and evaluateStreakOnLoad() mutates state as part of its check (consumes a freeze / resets streak), so the first version consumed two freezes for a single missed day. Fixed with a module-level one-time guard, documented in the code. Verified in-browser: streak-loss modal shows correct previous-streak count and resets to 0; Escape key closes it (added for 5.7).

features.name: Streak Freeze Mechanic

Badge only renders when inventory > 0, wired into Header.tsx next to StreakCounter. PRD notes freezes are 'earned via milestones, not purchased' — wired the earn path into 5.5 (streak milestones grant +1 freeze). Verified in-browser: seeded a 1-day-gap + 2-freeze scenario, confirmed streak preserved and inventory went to exactly 1 (not 0, after the Strict Mode double-invoke fix above).

New regenerateHearts() store action is called once on load and re-checked every 60s while the app stays open via ProgressInitializer.tsx — the periodic timer is just a re-check trigger, not the source of truth, so it satisfies 'not a running interval that resets on reload'. Verified in-browser: seeded 2/5 hearts with lastRegenAt 90 minutes in the past, reload correctly computed 3 regenerated hearts (90÷30) capped at max 5.

features.name: Progress HUD

Also displays XP, which required adding a new `xp: number` field to UserProgress (types/index.ts, lib/storage.ts) and an `addXP` store action — XP was not part of the original PRD/type-system scope; no drill exists yet (Phase 3) to actually award it, so it currently always renders 0.

features.name: Book/Chapter Memorization Path Picker

acceptance_criteria: All 66 canonical books listed, grouped by Old/New Testament
Selecting a book shows every chapter of that book
Selecting a chapter with authored content routes to /lesson/[nodeId]

features.notes: Not an originally scoped feature — added per explicit user request. Content scope limitation flagged to the user before building: the app only has authored verse content for 5 chapters (John 3, Psalm 23, Proverbs 3, Philippians 4, Romans 8), not the full Bible. Implemented the complete, accurate 66-book/chapter picker as requested; chapters without a matching VerseNode render disabled (native `disabled` attribute + muted styling + descriptive aria-label, e.g. "John chapter 1 — not yet available") rather than being hidden or leading to fake content. Added `book`/`chapter` fields to VerseNode and a new BibleBook type (types/index.ts) to support lookup. features.name: Verses-Per-Day Chapter Lesson Plans
features.description: After choosing a chapter, ask how many verses per day the user wants to memorize and generate a daily lesson tree from it. Each lesson (after the first) reviews previously learned verses in the chapter before teaching the new ones.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting an available chapter prompts for verses-per-day before showing a lesson list
Lesson tree is generated by chunking the chapter's verses into groups of the chosen size
Every lesson after the first includes a review pass over all previously learned verses in that chapter, followed by the full learn sequence for the new verses
Lessons unlock sequentially and progress persists across reloads
features.notes: Not an originally scoped feature — added per explicit user request, with content scope confirmed via clarifying question (user chose to author full verse-by-verse text for all 5 existing chapters rather than a single demo chapter or architecture-only stub). Authored 139 individual KJV verses (John 3: 36, Psalm 23: 6, Proverbs 3: 35, Philippians 4: 23, Romans 8: 39) in lib/chapterContent.ts from training knowledge of the public-domain KJV text — verse counts were verified programmatically against known chapter lengths, but the exact wording was not cross-checked against a reference Bible line-by-line, so there is elevated risk of minor wording drift, especially in less commonly quoted passages (e.g. Proverbs 3:19-35). Recommend spot-checking against a physical/official KJV before relying on this for real memorization. Reused the existing VerseSegment type ({id, reference, text}) for individual chapter verses rather than inventing a new type. Refactored lib/buildDrillPayload.ts to expose buildDrillPayloadForSegment so the new chapter-lesson flow reuses the exact same cloze/scramble/audio-mask generation logic as the original single-verse lessons, rather than duplicating it. Extracted the confetti animation out of LessonCompleteScreen.tsx into components/ui/Confetti.tsx (verse-agnostic primitive) so both completion screens share it. Bumped storage.ts SCHEMA_VERSION to 2 (adds chapterPlans to UserProgress) — existing saved progress from before this change resets to defaults via the existing schema-mismatch handling, by design. New chapter-lesson completions also increment the existing streak/XP/heart systems for consistency with the original lesson flow. Verified end-to-end in-browser: John 3 at 1 verse/day generates 36 lessons with correctly increasing review counts; completed Lesson 1 (cloze, sentence builder, first-letter, audio, final recitation) and confirmed Lesson 2 opens with a review-of-John-3:1 step before the new verse's learn sequence, matching the requested review-then-learn ordering. SUPERSEDED by 2.10: the user clarified the actual desired UX was substantially different (vertical day-path diagram, chained first-letter review, fixed 5-stage rep drills, speech recognition, boss battle, stickers), so this entire implementation (lib/lessonPlan.ts, ChapterLessonTree/SessionController/Loader/CompleteScreen.tsx, the lesson/[lessonNumber] route) was deleted and rebuilt — see 2.10.

features.name: Memorization Day Path (review chain, rep drills, speech recognition, boss battle, stickers)
features.description: Full rebuild of the chapter memorization flow per detailed user spec: Begin Memorizing entry point, book/chapter/version selection, a vertical day-path diagram, a chained first-letter review section, a fixed 5-stage rep-drill learning section per verse, a whole-chapter review day, a spoken boss-battle day, and a sticker-book reward.
acceptance_criteria: Home page has a Begin Memorizing CTA leading to book → chapter → version selection (KJV selectable, others visibly disabled)
Choosing verses/day generates a vertical, connected day-path diagram with a visual indicator of the current/next day and completed days filled green

Every learn day after the first opens with a chained review (type first letter of each word across all previously learned verses, live word reveal on correct letter, red flash + blocking retry on wrong letter, reference-typing checkpoints between verses, ending in an accuracy percentage) before teaching new verses

New-verse learning runs 5 stages per verse: speak it with the verse visible, type it with the verse visible, 3 rounds of tap-to-fill (round 1 blanks ~1/3 of the words, round 2 ~2/3, round 3 all of them, each round tapping the missing words in order from a word bank rather than dragging), type the whole verse one first letter at a time with each correct letter revealing its full word, then speak the whole verse blind
Wrong answers (typed or spoken) show a word-level diff against the correct verse rather than a generic error; the review chain shows the expected next letter
Days with more than one new verse insert a cumulative spoken group-recitation check after each verse beyond the first

A penultimate Chapter Review day drills first letters across the whole chapter then a spoken whole-chapter check; the final Boss Battle day requires a perfect spoken reference+verse recitation for every verse in sequence
Completing the boss battle shows a victory screen and awards a sticker visible on the Profile sticker book
features.notes:
This fully replaces feature 2.9's implementation (see its note) per the user's detailed follow-up spec — CLAUDE.md's own working agreement says a deviation gets documented rather than silently reinterpreted, and this is large enough that it's recorded as its own feature rather than an edit to 2.9's notes. Used EnterPlanMode given the size (new data model, ~28 new/changed files, a new browser capability) and confirmed two open questions with the user before building: (1) speech recognition has no cross-browser fallback — built against the Web Speech API (Chrome/Edge only), feature-detected so it disables gracefully rather than crashing on unsupported browsers, with no typed-input substitute, per the user's explicit choice; (2) the version selector is real, not a placeholder — KJV selectable, NIV/ESV/NASB/NLT visibly listed but disabled, mirroring the existing disabled-chapter pattern. Reused VerseSegment (not a new per-verse type), lib/chapterContent.ts's verse data untouched, lib/textMatch.ts's fuzzyMatch reused as-is for speech-transcript matching (already normalizes case/punctuation/whitespace — the same caveat about un-verified exact KJV wording from 2.9 still applies here since drills match against that same authored text). Two interpretive calls made and stated here rather than silently assumed: the accuracy formula is (totalWords − wordsWrong) / totalWords, counting each word wrong once no matter how many retries it took; and the reference-typing checkpoint appears before every verse in a review chain, including the first, not just between verses. The group-recitation and chapter-wide spoken checks default to 1 rep (spec didn't give an explicit count for those, unlike the fixed 5/5/5/3/3 per-verse sequence). No heart loss anywhere in this new flow — it's retry-until-correct/mastery-gated by design, matching the spec's description, unlike the original /learn skill-tree flow which still uses hearts unchanged. Bumped storage.ts SCHEMA_VERSION to 3 (adds stickers, restructures chapterPlans with version+completedDays) — existing saved progress resets via the existing schema-mismatch handling, same accepted precedent as before. Fixed one bug caught during verification: DayPathDiagram initially reused the app's existing bg-mastery-500 (purple) token for completed days out of habit — the user's spec explicitly says green, so it was changed to bg-brand-600 (the app's actual green). Verified in-browser end-to-end: Begin Memorizing → Psalms → 23 → KJV → 2 verses/day generates the correct 5-node path (3 learn days + Chapter Review + Boss Battle); Day 1 skips review and runs the full 5-phase rep sequence for Psalm 23:1 (confirmed each phase transition, and the first-letter phase's red-flash-then-reveal behavior with a deliberate wrong letter); Day 2 opens with the review chain (reference checkpoint → word-by-word reveal, same red-flash/retry behavior confirmed); Chapter Review and Boss Battle days render correctly when reached; the sticker book renders awarded stickers with correct chapter labels. Speech recognition itself could not be verified with a real spoken pass — the Browser pane blocks microphone access — but clicking the mic button was confirmed to fail gracefully (resolves to an empty transcript, shows a retry prompt) rather than crashing or hanging, which is the one thing that was testable without live audio. FOLLOW-UP FIXES from user testing: (1) real bug — the JSX for LearnVerseStage inside DaySessionController had no key tied to verse id, so on multi-verse days React reused the same component instance across verses instead of remounting it; phaseIndex (and the nested SpeakRep's completedReps) carried over from the previous verse, which is why verse 2 opened straight on 'Speak' and only needed one rep instead of three. Fixed with key={step.verse.id}. (2) Removed the write-with-no-scaffold phase that used to run immediately after Read, per explicit request — the per-verse sequence is now read x5 → first-letter-scaffold write x5 → write x3 → speak x3 (the remaining write phase absorbed the 'blind write' label since it's now the only from-memory typing step). (3) lib/textMatch.ts gained diffWords (positional word-level comparison against the target) and a new components/drills/MistakeDiff.tsx to render it; wired into WriteRep, FirstLetterWriteRep, and SpeakRep so a wrong answer shows the correct verse with the specific mismatched word(s) highlighted, and ReviewChain now shows the expected letter inline on a wrong keystroke instead of a generic message. (4) lib/speechRecognition.ts rewritten from a one-shot listenOnce() to startListening(onInterim), using continuous:true + interimResults:true so recognition no longer auto-stops on a short pause between words or sentences; SpeakRep now shows the live transcript as it's recognized and exposes a manual Stop button instead of the mic auto-ending the attempt. (5) Speech-transcript matching switched from exact fuzzyMatch to a new looseMatch (lib/textMatch.ts wordMatchRatio, 85% word-match threshold) for all SpeakRep-based checks, since the user reported the browser's recognition engine — a real, inherent limitation of the Web Speech API, not something in this app's control — frequently mis-transcribes individual words; typed drills (WriteRep, FirstLetterWriteRep, ReviewChain) still require an exact match since those test actual memorization rather than microphone/engine accuracy. Verified all five fixes in-browser: faked the SpeechRecognition constructor (since the Browser pane still can't grant real mic access) to confirm a 2-verse day now correctly cycles Read→First Letters→Write→Speak per verse with fresh rep counts each time; confirmed the mistake diff renders with the wrong word bolded/underlined on a deliberate wrong submission; confirmed looseMatch passes a transcript with 2 of 16 words altered (87.5%) and correctly fails/shows the diff on a nonsense transcript; confirmed ReviewChain's new expected-letter hint text on a wrong keystroke. STRUCTURAL REDESIGN: each "learn" day is no longer a single circle — it's 4 sequentially-unlocked sections (Review, Learn, Test, Pop Quiz), each its own circle in DayPathDiagram (extracted to DaySectionCluster.tsx) with its own route (/chapter/[book]/[chapterNum]/day/[dayNumber]/[section]) and its own lock state via ChapterPlanProgress.sectionsCompleted (dayNumber -> completed DaySectionKind[]; lib/dayPlan.ts's isSectionUnlocked checks that every prior section in DAY_SECTION_ORDER is done). chapter_review/boss_battle days are unchanged single circles — the 4-section split only applies to regular learn days per the request. Review reuses ReviewChain unchanged, except Day 1 (and any day with zero prior verses) now shows an explicit 'Nothing to review yet' screen with a Continue button instead of rendering an empty chain (ReviewChain returns null when there's nothing to review, which would have been a silent dead-end otherwise). Learn reuses the existing per-verse rep sequence + group-recitation-check logic (moved from the old monolithic DaySessionController into a new LearnSection.tsx, unchanged in behavior). Test and Pop Quiz are explicit placeholders (TestSectionPlaceholder.tsx, PopQuizSectionPlaceholder.tsx) that say plainly there's nothing there yet — matching the user's own 'this currently has nothing in it' framing for Test, extended the same way to Pop Quiz since its real mechanic (a random push notification to the user's phone, with a 5-minute countdown to respond) needs infrastructure this app doesn't have and wasn't part of this request: real cross-app push notification requires a service worker, a push subscription, VAPID keys, and something server-side to trigger sends at random times while the app is closed, which is a genuinely separate build (this app is still 100% client-side/localStorage, no backend). Did not attempt a fake or partial version of that — flagged it instead of silently building something that wouldn't match what was asked for. Finishing the 4th (last) section still runs the same day-completion logic as before (completeDay, XP, streak increment, streak-milestone check) via a trimmed-down DaySessionController that now only handles chapter_review/boss_battle; a parallel DaySectionController handles the per-section completion + transition screens for learn days. Bumped SCHEMA_VERSION to 4 for the sectionsCompleted addition to ChapterPlanProgress, same reset-on-mismatch precedent as before. Fixed two ESLint react-hooks/static-components errors caught by npm run lint: DayPathDiagram and DaySectionCluster were both selecting a Lucide icon component into a local variable inside render (`const Icon = ...`) and rendering it inline, which the linter flags because a locally-assigned component reference isn't guaranteed stable across renders — replaced both with small dedicated icon subcomponents (DayStatusIcon, SectionStatusIcon) declared outside the parent's render. Verified in-browser end-to-end on Psalm 23 at 2 verses/day: every learn day renders as 4 circles under one 'Day N' + verse-reference label; only Review is unlocked on a fresh Day 1, the rest show lock icons; completing Review (via its empty-state Continue button) unlocks Learn only, not Test/Pop Quiz; used the auto-complete button to clear Learn, then manually completed Test and Pop Quiz's placeholder Continue buttons; completing Pop Quiz (the last section) correctly fired 'Day 1 complete!' with streak 0→1 and XP 0→30, and returning to the path showed Day 1 fully green (checkmarks on all 4) with Day 2's Review circle now unlocked and Day 3 plus Chapter Review/Boss Battle still fully locked. FURTHER FOLLOW-UP: (1) added components/ui/AutoCompleteButton.tsx, a testing-only affordance (dashed border, muted styling, flask icon) wired into every rep/drill component (ReadRep, WriteRep, FirstLetterWriteRep, SpeakRep, ReviewChain) that immediately calls that component's onComplete, skipping all remaining reps/validation for that section — composite stages (ChapterReviewStage, BossBattleStage, GroupRecitationCheck) get it for free since they render these components directly. It's always visible (not gated behind an env flag) since the app has no production deployment yet and this is explicitly for the user's own testing. (2) ReviewChain rebuilt per explicit request: removed the per-verse reference-typing checkpoint entirely (previously required typing e.g. '23:2' between verses), and flattened all review verses into one continuous word stream — the first-letter chain now runs straight through every previously-learned verse back-to-back with no interruption, and the revealed-words display grows as one continuous block spanning verse boundaries instead of resetting per verse. The current verse's reference is still shown as a passive label ('Now in: Psalm 23:2') that updates automatically as the chain crosses into a new verse, since the user asked only to remove the typing requirement, not the reference context entirely. Accuracy scoring unchanged in spirit (same (total − wrong)/total formula) but now keyed by a single combined word index instead of a per-verse composite key, since there's no longer a verse-segmented structure to key against. Verified in-browser: auto-complete blitzed an entire 2-verse Day 1 (8 rep-phases plus the group-recitation check) in a handful of clicks straight to 'Day 1 complete!'; Day 2's review chain opens directly on the letter input with no reference prompt, and typing through all of Psalm 23:1 flows straight into 23:2 with the revealed text staying as one unbroken block and the 'Now in' label updating automatically. LATEST FOLLOW-UP: (1) removed the XP system entirely per explicit request ("for now" — treated as a real removal, not a feature flag, per this repo's established no-flags convention) — deleted the xp field from UserProgress, the addXP store action, its Header.tsx display, and every award call across DaySessionController, DaySectionController, and the original /learn flow's LessonSessionController (which also awarded XP per drill pass and on mastery). Bumped SCHEMA_VERSION to 5 for the UserProgress shape change, same reset-on-mismatch precedent as before. Grepped the whole app afterward to confirm zero remaining xp/addXP references. (2) Learn section rebuilt from the old 4-phase rep system (read/first-letter/write/speak, each repeated 3-5x) into the 3 stages the user specified: Stage 1 types the whole verse with it visible on screen (WriteRep reused with a new showVerse prop, 1 pass, not 5 — the new spec gives no repeat count so none was assumed); Stage 2 is 3 rounds of fill-in-the-blank (new components/drills/ClozeFillRound.tsx + lib/clozeRounds.ts's getBlankIndicesForRound, which interleaves blanks by word-index modulo 3 so round 1/2/3 blank indices 0,3,6.../1,4,7.../2,5,8... respectively — every word gets blanked exactly once across the 3 rounds); Stage 3 is a single spoken check of the full verse (SpeakRep reused, reps dropped from 3 to 1 to match "you must say the full verse," not repeated). Deleted ReadRep.tsx and FirstLetterWriteRep.tsx as dead code once LearnVerseStage.tsx stopped referencing them (confirmed via a repo-wide search first that nothing else imported either). The multi-verse "say them together" group-recitation checkpoint (GroupRecitationCheck, inserted after each verse beyond the first) was left untouched — the request confirmed it stays, and it lives in LearnSection.tsx's step-sequencing, which this change didn't touch. Verified in-browser end-to-end on a 2-verse Psalm 23 day: Header no longer shows XP anywhere, including on the Day-complete screen; Stage 1 shows the verse and requires exactly 1 correct submission; Stage 2 Round 1 on a 9-word verse correctly blanked indices 0/3/6 ("The"/"my"/"shall"), Round 2 correctly blanked 1/4/7, and a deliberately wrong entry revealed the correct missing word; auto-complete-blitzed through the remaining rounds and Stage 3 for verse 1, confirmed verse 2 started fresh at Stage 1 (no state bleed from the earlier key={step.verse.id} fix), confirmed a 16-word verse split into 6/5/5 blanks across its 3 rounds, and confirmed the group-recitation checkpoint still appears after verse 2 before the day completes; completing the full day still fired "Day 1 complete!" with the streak incrementing and no XP/crash.

LATEST FOLLOW-UP (Test zone removed, Learn redesigned to 5 stages): Per user request, the Test day-section was removed entirely (not hidden behind a flag) -- DaySectionKind dropped "test" from its union, DAY_SECTION_ORDER in lib/dayPlan.ts now reads [review, learn, pop_quiz], DaySectionCluster/DaySectionController no longer reference it, and TestSectionPlaceholder.tsx was deleted. Each day now shows exactly 3 circles: Review, Learn, Pop Quiz. The Learn section's per-verse flow was rebuilt from 3 stages to 5, replacing the prior type-with-view -> 3x typed-cloze -> speak sequence: Stage 1 speaks the verse while it stays visible on screen (added a showVerse prop to SpeakRep, mirroring the prop WriteRep already had); Stage 2 types the verse while visible (reused WriteRep with showVerse, unchanged from before); Stage 3 is 3 rounds of drag-and-drop instead of typed fill-in-the-blank -- lib/dragDropRounds.ts's getDragDropIndicesForRound(totalWords, round) blanks words where i % 3 < round, so round 1 blanks ~1/3 of the words, round 2 cumulatively blanks ~2/3 (adds another third on top of round 1's blanks rather than swapping to a different third), and round 3 blanks all of them -- matching the user's "round 1 removes 33%, round 2 adds another 33%, round 3 removes all" spec exactly. Each round is a fresh DragDropRound mount (keyed by round) so the blank/placed state resets between rounds. The old typed-cloze mechanic (lib/clozeRounds.ts, components/drills/ClozeFillRound.tsx) is now obsolete for this flow and was deleted rather than left dead. DragDropRound renders the verse as a flex-wrap paragraph of static words and dashed drop-target spans (each tagged data-slot-index), plus a shuffled tray of DragWordTile components below it. DragWordTile wraps a Framer Motion motion.div with drag, dragSnapToOrigin, and dragElastic so an incorrect drop simply springs back to the tray with no state change (playIncorrectSfx fires but nothing else happens). On a correct drop the tile's original word-index is added to a placed Set, which both removes it from the tray and swaps the target slot to show the real word; when the placed set covers every blank index for that round, onComplete() advances to the next round/stage. Drop-target hit-testing uses document.elementsFromPoint(x, y) (the full z-order stack at the drop point, not just the topmost element) filtered down to the first element carrying data-slot-index -- this sidesteps the dragged tile itself (which carries no such attribute) shadowing the slot underneath it at drop time, without needing any pointer-events trickery. Stage 4 types the whole verse against a first-letter scaffold (new FirstLetterTypeRep.tsx -- shows each word with only its first letter kept and the rest of its alphabetic characters replaced with underscores, punctuation preserved as-is, then a textarea validated with fuzzyMatch against the full verse, same mistake-diff-on-wrong pattern as WriteRep). Stage 5 speaks the whole verse blind, reusing SpeakRep exactly as it behaved before this phase (showVerse omitted/false). The multi-verse group-recitation checkpoint between verses in LearnSection.tsx was untouched -- out of scope for this request. Verified in-browser end to end: walked a fresh Day 1 through Review -> all 5 Learn stages -> confirmed Pop Quiz is the section unlocked next, with the day-path screen showing only Review/Learn/Pop Quiz circles for every day (no Test circle anywhere, including the Chapter Review and Boss Battle days, which were already single-section and unaffected). Confirmed round 1/2/3 blank counts against a 14-word verse (John 3:1) matched the i % 3 < round formula exactly (5, then 10, then all 14 blanked). Confirmed the drop-target hit-testing resolves each slot's own on-screen coordinates back to itself via elementsFromPoint. Genuine end-to-end mouse/touch dragging through Framer Motion's gesture recognizer could not be reliably faked with synthetic pointer events in the sandboxed Browser pane (Framer's PanSession did not register a drag from either a single-jump left_click_drag or a scripted multi-step PointerEvent sequence), so that specific interaction -- an actual finger/mouse drag completing successfully -- should be spot-checked by the user in a real browser; the underlying index math and drop-target resolution it depends on were verified directly. npm run build and npm run lint both passed clean with zero errors after all changes.

LATEST FOLLOW-UP (Stage 3 drag-and-drop replaced with tap-to-fill; Stage 4 reworked to per-word first-letter reveal): user found the drag interaction not to their liking and asked for a click-based alternative, plus asked Stage 4 to work by typing one letter at a time with each correct letter popping the full word into view, rather than typing the whole verse into a textarea against a static scaffold. Stage 3: lib/dragDropRounds.ts was renamed to lib/wordBankRounds.ts (same cumulative i % 3 < round blanking logic, unchanged), and components/drills/DragDropRound.tsx + DragWordTile.tsx were deleted and replaced by components/drills/WordBankRound.tsx. The verse still renders as static words plus dashed blank spans, and the word bank tray below it still holds the missing words shuffled -- but tiles are now plain buttons instead of Framer Motion drag handles. Blanks must be filled strictly left-to-right: clicking a tray tile compares its word text against words[blankIndices[placedCount]] (the next not-yet-filled blank in verse order); a match consumes that tile and advances placedCount, revealing the word in its slot; a mismatch flashes that specific tile red (bg-heart-500, tracked via a wrongTileId state) and does nothing else -- no elementsFromPoint hit-testing or drag gesture recognition needed anymore, which also removes the earlier phase's noted gap where genuine mouse/touch dragging couldn't be verified in the sandboxed Browser pane. features.name: Spaced Repetition for Memorized Verses
features.description: Once a path (book/chapter/verse/topic) is fully completed, its verses move into the Memorized section as contiguous per-chapter entities — merging with an already-memorized neighboring verse where one exists — each independently tracked by a fixed-cadence spaced repetition schedule (daily for a week, then weekly for a month, then monthly indefinitely) that surfaces what's due for long-term review.
acceptance_criteria: A path's verses only enter the Memorized section once the entire path is finished (every day through the final boss-battle day), not incrementally as each verse is learned
When a newly-memorized verse is immediately before or after an already-memorized verse in the same book+chapter, it merges into that verse's entity rather than becoming a separate one
Entities never span more than one chapter — merging is scoped to book+chapter, so finishing one chapter's worth of verses and then starting a new chapter (or a new book) always begins a fresh entity

Each entity carries its own fixed-cadence spaced repetition schedule (daily for the first 7 successful reviews, weekly for the next 4, then monthly forever after) independent of the path-level day-to-day Review section — a failed review drops the schedule back to daily
The Memorized Verses page shows which verse groups are currently due for review and lets the user start a review session that walks through them one at a time
A verse reached via two different paths (e.g. a chapter path and a topic that happens to include one of its verses) is tracked as a single shared entity, not duplicated
features.notes:
User request (verbatim, across two messages): "After a verse/verses are memorized and reviewed in the path then it gets added to the 'memorized' section, within the memorized section create a spaced repetition system that determines what verses need reviewing. Whenever new verses are added to the memorized section always first check to see if the verse before/after is already there, if so add it to that entity for the SRS do this only up to a full chapter, after that they start a new chapter" -- then, mid-implementation, a clarifying correction: "After a path is complete have the book, chapter or verse(s) move to the memorized section where it enters a Spaced review system that determines what verses need reviewing." The second message simplified the trigger from an incremental 'verse learned + one more day completed' condition (my first-pass reading) to the simpler, stricter rule actually implemented: a path's verses all move to Memorized together, only once the whole path -- including its final boss-battle day -- is done. This lines up with the existing sticker system, which already awards on that same boss-battle-complete event, so a fully memorized path always gets both a sticker and its verses added to the SRS pool at once. 

Structural prerequisite: VerseSegment previously only carried a human-readable reference string (e.g. "John 3:16") and an id slug -- not enough to reliably group verses by book+chapter+number for merging (parsing it back out of the reference string is lossy for Psalms, where the display label reads "Psalm" singular but the real book name is "Psalms"). Added explicit book/chapter/verseNumber fields to VerseSegment instead, set once at each construction site (lib/chapterContent.ts's buildVerseSegments, and by hand across the 11 topic verses in lib/memorizationContent.ts) rather than parsed at read time. 

lib/memorizedEntities.ts's addVerseToEntities is the merge algorithm: for a newly-memorized verse, look for an existing entity in the same book+chapter whose endVerse is one less (predecessor) or whose startVerse is one more (successor); extend/bridge into either, both, or neither. Entities are scoped to book+chapter by construction, so the 'cap at a full chapter, start fresh for the next chapter' part of the request falls out naturally -- there's no explicit cap to enforce since verse numbers can't exceed the chapter's real length, and cross-chapter adjacency is never checked at all. syncMemorizedEntities rebuilds the full entity list from scratch off current path progress every time (cheap at this app's scale, and avoids incremental-diff bugs): an entity's id encodes its exact range (e.g. "John|3|1-2"), so a range that didn't change keeps its previous SRS schedule via that same id, while a range that just grew via a merge gets a fresh SRS schedule under its new id -- content changed, so its review history resets. This sync runs inside the store's completeDay action, the only action that can push a path across the 'fully complete' threshold. 

lib/srs.ts is a freshly authored SM-2-style scheduler (the original lib/srs.ts from the old skill-tree flow was deleted earlier this session along with the rest of that system) -- deliberately simplified to a pass/fail signal rather than SM-2's classic 0-5 quality grade, because every review mechanic already in this app (ReviewChain, BossBattleStage, SpeakRep) is retry-until-correct with no concept of a graded or failed attempt; matching that, an SRS review always resolves as a pass once SpeakRep's loose-match recitation succeeds, and the interval simply grows (1 day -> 6 days -> previous interval * easiness factor). 

Because entities are keyed by the verse's actual book+chapter+number rather than by which path reached it, a verse memorized via two different paths (for instance a chapter path and a topic that happens to include one of that chapter's verses) collapses into one shared entity instead of being tracked twice -- an emergent property of the design, not special-cased. 

UI: a new 'Spaced Review' card on /memorized (SrsOverview.tsx) lists verse groups currently due and links to /memorized/review, which steps through them one at a time via SrsReviewSession.tsx (reusing SpeakRep for a blind spoken recitation of each entity's full range) and calls the new recordSrsReview store action after each. This is a distinct, separate concept from the existing 'Continue Daily Review' button on the same page, which is about a path's own short-term day-to-day Review section during active learning -- the Spaced Review card is long-term maintenance for verses that have already graduated out of active learning. 

Verified in-browser end to end: completed the full 3-day path (learn -> full review -> boss battle) for John 3:1 as its own verse-path and confirmed it created a single-verse memorized entity with a freshly-due SRS schedule; then completed the same full path for John 3:2 as a separate verse-path and confirmed the two merged into one John|3|1-2 entity (not two separate ones); confirmed /memorized's Spaced Review card listed exactly 'John 3:1-2' as due; ran the review session (SpeakRep's Auto-complete testing button, standing in for real speech input as established earlier this session) and confirmed the entity's SRS state advanced correctly (repetitionCount 0->1, intervalDays 0->1, nextDueAt pushed to tomorrow) and the due list correctly emptied to 'All caught up!' afterward. Schema bumped 7->8 for the new memorizedEntities field, resetting existing local progress per the same accepted precedent used at every prior schema change this session. npm run build and npm run lint both passed clean.

Follow-up user request (verbatim): "Make it so that once verses enter the SRS they are reviewed everyday for a week, then once a week for a month, then once a month." Replaced the original SM-2-style growing-interval algorithm in lib/srs.ts (interval = previous interval * easiness factor, unbounded growth) with a fixed three-tier cadence keyed off repetitionCount: reviews 1-7 use a 1-day interval (daily for a week), reviews 8-11 use a 7-day interval (four more reviews ≈ a month of weekly review), and review 12 onward use a fixed 30-day interval (monthly, indefinitely) — tier boundaries picked so the counts line up with the request's own "a week" / "a month" framing rather than counting literal calendar days. A failed review still resets repetitionCount to 0 and drops back to a 1-day interval, matching the existing 'retry relearns from the top' pattern used everywhere else in the app. Since easinessFactor was only ever read by the old growth formula, it was removed from SRSState entirely (types/index.ts) rather than left unused — confirmed via repo-wide grep that nothing else referenced it. Schema bumped 9->10 since SRSState's persisted shape changed, resetting existing local progress per the same accepted precedent used at every prior schema change this session. Verified by seeding memorizedEntities directly in localStorage and stepping through recordSrsReview via the review session's Auto-complete button at both tier boundaries: repetitionCount 7->8 correctly switched intervalDays from 1 to 7, and repetitionCount 11->12 correctly switched intervalDays from 7 to 30 (and stays there on further reviews, since the fallback branch is unbounded). npm run build and npm run lint both passed clean.

features.notes:
User request (verbatim): "Now lets make the system so that all books and chapters in 5 different versions are available to be chosen. Make it so that its least intesteive on the code, maybe a download externally when chosing." 

Before building, flagged a real constraint: NIV/ESV/NASB/NLT are modern copyrighted translations with no free, key-less API — asked the user how to proceed. They chose to use api.bible (scripture.api.bible) with their own API key, added later (not available during this session), so the server route and error states were built and verified against the *absence* of a key rather than live translated text. 

Architecture, kept deliberately minimal per the request: previously only 5 hand-picked chapters had any verse text at all (hardcoded in lib/chapterContent.ts, KJV only) — every other book/chapter was grayed out. lib/bibleBooks.ts already had accurate chapter counts for all 66 books, so no book/chapter *metadata* fetching was ever needed — only verse *text* needed to become fetchable, which is the single narrow thing this change actually does. 

app/api/bible/chapter/route.ts is a server-only Next.js Route Handler (the only place BIBLE_API_KEY is ever read — never sent to the browser). It resolves our internal version code (KJV/NIV/ESV/NASB/NLT) to whatever bibleId that translation has in the caller's api.bible account by searching GET /v1/bibles?language=eng for a matching abbreviation/name (cached in-memory per server process, since account bibleIds aren't fixed UUIDs we can hardcode), then fetches GET /v1/bibles/{bibleId}/chapters/{USFM}.{chapter}?content-type=html&include-verse-numbers=true and parses the verse-number <span> markers out of the returned HTML into a plain per-verse text array. HTML content-type was chosen over api.bible's plain-text mode specifically because the verse-number span is an unambiguous, documented boundary to split on — the plain-text mode concatenates verse numbers directly against the following word with no reliable separator, which would make splitting fragile. This parsing could not be tested against real translated text in this session (no live key) — flagged clearly to the user to spot-check once their key is added, with the regex isolated to one function (parseChapterHtml) if it needs adjusting. 

Caching: lib/bibleContentCache.ts is a separate localStorage key (verses:bibleContentCache) from verses:progress on purpose — it's fetched content, not user progress, so it isn't versioned or reset by the progress schema's SCHEMA_VERSION bump mechanism. It's keyed by book+chapter only, not version — a deliberate simplification matching the app's existing one-version-per-pathKey design (a given book+chapter path already only ever has one PathProgress.version at a time), accepted as a documented tradeoff rather than threading a version dimension through the whole cache and every downstream reader. 

lib/chapterContent.ts's getChapterVerses(book, chapter) changed from a static lookup into a pure, synchronous cache read — it returns undefined until lib/bibleApiClient.ts's ensureChapterLoaded has fetched that chapter at least once. This let every existing downstream consumer (lib/progressSummary.ts's day-plan/review-due/memorized-verses functions, SrsReviewSession, MemorizedStats) keep working completely unchanged, since by the time a path exists in the store its content is guaranteed already fetched. The only real ripple was at the two entry points: app/path/[key]/page.tsx and .../day/[dayNumber]/page.tsx are Next.js Server Components and cannot read localStorage at all, so they were simplified to call a new resolvePathLabel(key) (pure, no cache dependency — computes a path's display label from just its book/chapter/verse numbers, no verse text needed) instead of the old verses-returning resolvePath, and verse resolution moved client-side into PathOverviewScreen.tsx and DayLoader.tsx (each now resolves from cache, or calls lib/bibleApiClient.ts's ensurePathVerses as a fallback fetch, with loading/error UI via the new components/ui/FetchStatus.tsx). 

GuidedPathFlow.tsx now fetches-then-navigates for all three modes: Chapter mode fetches one chapter; Verse mode fetches one chapter then shows the verse grid from the real fetched verse count (previously VersePicker.tsx's grid length came from data that only existed for 5 hardcoded chapters); Book mode fetches every chapter of the book via lib/fetchWithConcurrency.ts (concurrency capped at 4, with a per-chapter loading label) before navigating — a real, disclosed scalability caveat: a 150-chapter book like Psalms means 150 sequential-ish requests and, once loaded, a 150+ lesson day-plan, which was already a latent property of Book mode's one-lesson-per-verse design and is now actually reachable instead of only ever running for single-chapter books. 

Book mode also gained a version-picker step it never had before (it previously navigated immediately, hardcoded to "KJV"), and Verse mode gained one too (previously skipped straight from chapter to verse grid, silently KJV) — both fixed in passing since the infrastructure now exists and the user asked for all 5 versions to be available everywhere, not just in Chapter mode. VersionPicker.tsx's props were generalized from book+chapter to a single title string to support this reuse across all three modes. BookList.tsx and ChapterGrid.tsx had their availableBooks/availableChapters gating props and disabled-button branches deleted outright (not left as dead code) since every book and chapter is selectable now that content is fetched on demand rather than pre-authored. 

Verified in-browser end to end without a live key: all 66 books (including previously-unavailable ones like Genesis) render as fully selectable with no grayed-out entries; Genesis's ChapterGrid correctly shows all 50 chapters selectable; Chapter, Book, and Verse mode all correctly reach a VersionPicker step listing all 5 versions enabled; selecting a version in each mode correctly hits GET /api/bible/chapter, receives the expected 501 with a clear "no BIBLE_API_KEY configured" message, and surfaces it through FetchError with a working Try again retry button rather than crashing or hanging; confirmed the same graceful error also appears when navigating directly to a pre-existing in-progress path whose content isn't in the new cache (the ensurePathVerses fallback-fetch path on PathOverviewScreen/DayLoader), rather than showing broken/empty content. npm run build and npm run lint both passed clean with zero errors.

features.name: Book Mode: Verses/Day + Sliding-Window/Rotation/Weekly/Monthly Review
features.description: Book mode now asks how many verses per day once its content is fetched, chunks lessons accordingly, and reviews with a distinct spaced-repetition-like schedule scoped to book mode only: each lesson reviews the previous chapter in full plus the current chapter's progress so far, plus one chapter cycling through a 7-slot daily rotation; every 8 chapters that graduate out of daily rotation form a weekly-review batch (shown as its own circle), and each superseded weekly batch is absorbed into an ever-growing monthly review.

Once a chapter is no longer covered by that sliding window, it joins a 7-chapter daily rotation (a ring buffer that never empties) reviewed one chapter at a time, round robin

Every time an 8th chapter would need to join daily rotation, the oldest of the 7 evicts into a separate, growing weekly-batch accumulator — once 8 have accumulated, that batch becomes the active weekly review, shown as its own circle on a fixed cadence
When a second batch of 8 chapters completes and becomes the new weekly review, the previous weekly batch is promoted into an ever-growing monthly review bucket instead of disappearing
This entire system is scoped to book-mode paths only — chapter/verse/topic paths are completely unaffected, still one verse per lesson reviewing everything learned so far

The path diagram labels multi-verse lessons with a verse range (e.g. "Genesis 1:1-5", or "Philippians 3:21–Philippians 4:4" when a chunk crosses a chapter boundary) and gives weekly/monthly review circles their own distinct icon
features.notes:
User request (verbatim): "For memorizing a book lets make it a bit different. When they chose the book they chose a number of verses per day. The lessons now get split into this amount of verses. For the review part of the lesson, they review all previous verses starting at the beginning of the previous chapter, for example if todays verse is Gen 4:3, the review section is Gen 3:1-4:2. Once a chapter leaves this review section (like Gen 1&2) it gets added to a daily rotation included in the review section that reviews one previous chapter, so for Gen 4:3 it may be chapter 1, then the next day it goes to chapter 2, and then back to chapter 1. Once 8 Chapters are Complete, these chapters get bunched together and reviewed on a weekly basis. This review is added as a separate circle when applicable. Any new chapters that are added to the daily rotation after this replace the earliest added chapter, for ex ch 8 would replace ch 1, ch 9 would replace ch 2, etc. If a book completes another 8 chapters the original 8 chapters are now added to a monthly review and the new 8 chapters are added to a weekly review. This goes until the book is complete." Then, mid-implementation, a clarifying follow-up: "The weekly review of 8 chapters is seperate from the daily."

The spec had one genuine internal ambiguity worth surfacing before building: "once 8 chapters are complete, bunched into weekly" reads as the daily pool filling to 8 and emptying, while "ch8 replaces ch1, ch9 replaces ch2" reads as a ring buffer that never empties. Asked the user directly; they clarified the daily pool caps at 7 (not 8) specifically because the previous chapter is already covered by the sliding window and doesn't need its own rotation slot, and confirmed it never empties. Cap 7 resolves the arithmetic exactly as given: departure 8 evicts departure 1, departure 9 evicts departure 2, etc. Their later message confirmed the weekly-batch-of-8 accumulator is a separate track from the 7-slot daily ring buffer, not the same pool relabeled -- exactly what had already been designed from the cap-7 resolution.

Algorithm (lib/bookReviewSchedule.ts): chapters depart the sliding window in order as the book progresses (chapter K departs at the first lesson whose anchor chapter exceeds K+1). Departures feed a 7-slot FIFO ring buffer (the daily rotation) that never empties; once full, each new arrival evicts the oldest member into a separate weekly-batch accumulator. Once that accumulator reaches 8, it becomes the current weekly-review batch and resets; if a currentWeeklyBatch already existed at that point, it gets folded into the (ever-growing) monthly bucket first. lib/bookDayPlan.ts chunks verses into versesPerDay-sized lessons, computes the sliding-window review (previous chapter in full + current chapter up to the chunk's first verse) plus one rotation chapter chosen round-robin from the daily pool for that lesson, and inserts weekly_review days every 7 lessons (once a batch exists) and monthly_review days every 30 (once the monthly bucket is non-empty) -- cadences chosen to fit this app's existing lesson-indexed "day" convention (a lesson-count, not a real calendar day, matching how every other day-plan in the app already works) since the user's own "weekly"/"monthly" wording doesn't map to literal calendar time here.

Verified end-to-end two ways: (1) a temporary debug route (deleted before finishing) fed the real buildBookDayPlan a synthetic 40-chapter book and confirmed the full lifecycle exactly -- chapters 1-8 became the weekly batch, repeated on the 7-lesson cadence, then correctly promoted to monthly once chapters 9-16 completed and became the new weekly batch, and the monthly bucket kept growing (1-16) once a third batch (17-24) later superseded batch 2 as the active weekly. Rotation alternation (chapter1, chapter2, chapter1...) matched the user's own example exactly once pool cap 7 was in place. (2) Live-tested against real fetched KJV content: selected Philippians (4 chapters, 104 verses -- matching the real KJV verse count exactly, confirming the HTML-parsing pipeline from the prior phase works against live translated text), picked 5 verses/day, confirmed the resulting 21-lesson path diagram correctly range-labels multi-verse chunks ("Philippians 1:1-5") including one that crosses a chapter boundary ("Philippians 3:21–Philippians 4:4"), and opened lesson 1 to confirm the review section correctly shows "Nothing to review yet" (no prior chapter exists) followed by the real fetched verse text ("Paul and Timotheus, the servants of Jesus Christ...") in the Learn stage. Philippians itself is too short to exercise weekly/monthly review (needs 8+ completed chapters), which is expected and correctly absent from its diagram.

PathProgress gained an optional versesPerDay field (book-kind paths only); buildPathDayPlan(key, verses, plan) in lib/dayPlan.ts is the single dispatch point now used everywhere a day-plan is built (PathOverviewScreen, DayLoader, lib/progressSummary.ts's three functions) so book-mode paths get correct day counts for progress/review-due/memorized-verse detection instead of silently falling back to the generic one-verse-per-lesson plan. DaySessionController reuses the existing generic ReviewSection component for the two new day kinds (it was already purely driven by day.reviewVerses with no kind-checking, so no new review-rendering component was needed). Schema bumped 11->12 for the PathProgress shape change, resetting existing local progress per the established precedent used at every prior schema change this session. npm run build and npm run lint both passed clean.

features.notes: User pasted a real Crossway api.esv.org API key directly in chat, along with: "please make sure the proper safeties are in place as to not violate crossways conditions for it". Wrote the key to .env.local (gitignored, never echoed back in plaintext). Researched api.esv.org's actual terms of use via WebFetch (docs page + the standard published copyright notice) rather than relying on assumption, confirming: max 500 verses per query or per book stored locally (whichever is less, both figures apply — cap = min(500, floor(totalBookVerses/2))), non-commercial use only, and a required copyright notice + esv.org link wherever text is displayed. First pass (before this feature's final form) blocked ESV entirely for Book-mode selection, since fetching an entire book structurally can't fit under a half-book cap. The user pushed back mid-turn: "Instead of out right blocking the ESV book, make an different way of downlaoding and storing the verses so that it abides by the rules but you can still learn the book in ESV" — this was a real, reasonable request since Crossway's terms cap what's *locally stored*, not what's fetched or displayed, and their own docs explicitly anticipate apps 'periodically clearing cache'. Redesigned as a rolling LRU eviction cache: lib/esvCacheTracker.ts now tracks per-book chapters in least-recently-used order (not just counts); lib/bibleApiClient.ts's ensureChapterLoaded evicts the least-recently-used cached ESV chapter(s) for a book (via the new removeCachedChapter in bibleContentCache.ts) whenever a new fetch would push that book's persisted total over its cap, rather than refusing the fetch. This required fixing a correctness bug this design would otherwise introduce: lib/memorizationContent.ts's getBookVerses() requires ALL of a book's chapters to be simultaneously present in the persistent cache, which eviction structurally prevents for any book whose total exceeds the cap. Fixed by having ensurePathVerses's book branch build its return value directly from each ensureChapterLoaded call's own return value (verses are always correct even if immediately evicted afterward) instead of re-reading through resolvePath()'s cache-only aggregation. Also added an in-memory-only (never persisted to localStorage) session cache for assembled full-book results, keyed by version+book, so repeat navigation within the same tab visit doesn't re-fetch the whole book every time — this is compliant since Crossway's cap is specifically about persistent local storage, not transient in-memory state that dies with the tab. Verified live end-to-end in the browser: fetched real Mark 1 ESV text confirming the new key works; seeded a fake tracker value near the cap and confirmed the eviction math via a real Chapter-mode fetch; then did a full real run — Book mode, Mark, ESV, all 673 verses fetched successfully, tracker afterward showed only 337/339 verses persisted (8 of 16 chapters evicted), the 137-lesson day plan for the WHOLE book still resolved correctly despite most chapters being evicted, and opening Day 1's lesson showed real ESV text ('The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.') plus the required Crossway copyright/esv.org attribution notice.
